Mark Zuckerberg has published an article in The Wall Street Journal discussing concerns about superintelligent systems.

He warns that if just a few institutions hold highly advanced AI, they could gain disproportionate economic and political power. According to Zuckerberg, history shows that trusting a single powerful entity to act benevolently rarely produces safe or beneficial results.

Zuckerberg uses the example of one individual possessing a superintelligent lawyer. This scenario, he suggests, would create significant courtroom advantages even if the individual's case lacked merit, ultimately resulting in a less fair society.

He states that the future should benefit everyone and indicates plans to share further ideas on a positive path forward for superintelligence.

A group of 1,132 employees from major AI laboratories—including senior staff at OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta—have issued a warning about the risks of rapid, automated AI research. They state that accelerating AI development could push technological progress beyond the control of any individual or organization.

These experts are urging the United States government to establish coordinated technical and political measures with other nations. Their proposal calls for mechanisms capable of slowing AI advances intentionally, as no company or state is likely to step back from aggressive research on its own.

The group notes that current trends suggest technology may soon progress at a scale and speed that exceeds human understanding. They stress the importance of global cooperation and state that participation from China is essential for any effective response.

🖥 Microsoft launches AI for code vulnerability detection

Microsoft integrated MAI-Cyber-1-Flash into MDASH, an AI agent system that finds, verifies, and helps fix vulnerabilities in large codebases. The lightweight model handles up to 90% of tasks, while the toughest 10% go to GPT-5.4, speeding up protection and cutting costs.

The MAI-Cyber-1-Flash and GPT-5.4 combo scored 96% on CyberGym, 12 points above Mythos and better than Gemini and standalone GPT models. This setup also halves the cost compared to Microsoft’s previous system using GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4 mini, and GPT-5.3 Codex.

🇺🇸 The Pentagon is building AI data centers on at least a dozen military bases across the US.

The Army and Air Force are opening federal land to commercial developers in exchange for access to computing power.

Fort Bliss in Texas will host the Pentagon's first ever hyperscale data center.

🔍 Google Pixel 11 lineup details leak

Google plans to launch four Pixel 11 models: Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and 11 Pro Fold. Screen sizes and resolutions remain similar to the previous generation, but brightness will increase to 3100 nits on the base model and 3600 nits on Pro versions. The foldable model features dual screens with 3600 nits outside and 3500 nits inside.

The Pixel 11 series runs on the new Tensor G6 chip built on a 2nm TSMC process, featuring a seven-core CPU with an ARM C1-Ultra core at 4.11 GHz, PowerVR graphics, Titan M3 security chip, and MediaTek M90 modem. Storage starts at 256 GB, eliminating the 128 GB option and raising the entry price to match last year's 256 GB model.
